slides.headline: Big weekend of DIY, stiff back on Monday?
slides.sub: Why weekend projects strain backs, and how to plan the next one smarter.

slides.title: Why DIY catches backs out
slides.body: Most of us don't spend hours bending, twisting and carrying all week. Then Saturday brings garden beds, flat-packs and paint. The sudden jump in load is often the issue.

slides.title: The next 48 hours
slides.body: Keep moving gently. Short walks, changing positions often and heat for comfort can help. Most back strains like this settle over days to a couple of weeks.

slides.title: Break the job into chunks
slides.body: Work in 30 to 45 minute blocks, then switch tasks. Alternate lifting jobs with standing or walking jobs so your back isn't doing the same thing for hours.

slides.title: Set up to reduce the strain
slides.body: Kneel or use a low stool for ground-level work, keep heavy things close as you lift, and get a hand for the bulky stuff. Small changes spread the load.

slides.title: When to get it checked
slides.body: Pain spreading down a leg with numbness or weakness, pain that keeps getting worse, or bladder or bowel changes need medical attention. Head to your GP or emergency department.

slides.headline: Back still grumpy after the weekend?
slides.body: Our chiropractors assess how you move, use hands-on care where it helps and give you exercises to get back to your projects.

caption:
The garden looks great. Your back, less so.

Weekend DIY often means hours of bending, carrying and twisting that your back doesn't do the rest of the week. That jump in load is a common reason for a Monday strain. Most settle over days to a couple of weeks with gentle movement.

Next time, work in 30 to 45 minute blocks, switch between lifting and lighter jobs, kneel for ground-level work and get a hand with bulky items. Leg numbness or weakness, worsening pain, or bladder or bowel changes need medical attention.

story.headline: Big DIY weekend planned?
story.body: Work in 30 to 45 minute blocks and alternate heavy jobs with lighter ones. Your back will thank you.
